text:
Arjun: FYI the backfill running right now got a policy change rolled by infra (routing policy tightened). Jobs in-progress are seeing mid-run preemption and we're getting a deluge of alerts. Do we cancel in-flight or pause and resume?
Priya: Oof. Was that a manual tweak or an autopolicy rollout?
Miguel: Autopolicy rollout from last night (rate limit reweight for priority_lane). It doesn't retroactively apply to existing leases but the queue reconciler just enforced the stricter limits after a config reload.
Zoe: So leases granted earlier are being evicted when they try to renew tokens? That explains the spikes.
ops-bot: infra: routing-policy v3.1 deployed at 2026-03-15T03:12:04Z. Affected queues: priority_lane, shared-pool-2.
Arjun: We need a short term playbook: customers expect backfills to be resilient. My vote: pause the job, snapshot progress, re-evaluate route, then resume under either original policy or with a canary segment.
Priya: Pause+snapshot sounds safe. Do we have snapshot tooling that is consistent across Dedicated + Hosted?
Miguel: We have checkpoints but they are not portable across kernel variants or quant profiles. If runtime changes were part of the policy change we might get inconsistent results on resume.
Sam: Could add a run-level metadata tag 'policy_lock_version' and 'runtime_fingerprint' when job starts. If policy changes and fingerprint mismatches, refuse resume and require an explicit 'allow_resume_with_policy_change' flag.
Zoe: UX: console should show a diff of routing settings that changed + a callout ‘resuming may incur higher cost or fail’. Provide options: Cancel & refund window, Pause & await manual approval, Canary-resume for X% of tenants.
Arjun: Canary-resume is interesting: let 1% of tenants finish under new policy to validate. But we need API-level support: /v1/backfills/{id}/resume?mode=canary&pct=1
Miguel: Implementation complexity: the scheduler needs to tag shards for canary and route them to a separate allocation pool. Not trivial but doable.
Priya: For billing clarity we also need to attach an audit note: 'policy_change_id' and 'resume_mode' to invoices/tokens so customers can reconcile.
ops-bot: ops: backfill r-99a paused by operator at 2026-03-15T03:18:21Z. Snapshot saved: s-664.
Sam: Quick workaround: if pause+snapshot is already available, we can implement resume-gate that checks policy_lock_version == current_policy and runtime_fingerprint == current_runtime. If mismatch, require operator override with explicit reason. Keep override logged.
Zoe: That seems reasonable. Add an operator modal with text box for reason and a checkbox 'force resume despite policy/runtime mismatch'.
Arjun: For long-term, we should avoid surprise autopolicy rollouts touching queues with active long-running jobs. Suggest: autopolicy must include a 'quiesce' window flag: when present, changes are staged but not enforced for N minutes on queues with active leases.
Miguel: Agree. We can add 'staged_rollout' metadata to policy objects and have the reconciler skip enforcement for active-leased queues.
Priya: This is a cross-team change (infra + scheduler + console). Can we ship the pause/resume gating and audit fields fast, then follow up with staged_rollout?
Sam: Yes. Plan: 1) add resume API with mode param + audit fields; 2) add resume gating check for policy/runtime fingerprints; 3) console modal and canary slider; 4) staged_rollout RFC.
Zoe: I'll draft the console copy and modal mock. Need copy for the 'reason' logging and the cost delta warning.
Arjun: Miguel, can you add runtime_fingerprint to job metadata ASAP so we can start gating?
Miguel: On it. Will emit fields: kernel_variant, kv_cache_mode, quant_profile, model_variant.
ops-bot: infra: policy v3.2 scheduled canary for 2026-03-16T02:00:00Z (staged_rollout=false).
Priya: Note: we should also consider tenant opt-in for canary-resume. Some customers won’t accept changed routing/cost midbackfill. Add a tenant_policy_override boolean in the backfill create API.
Sam: Good call. Add field 'allow_policy_changes:boolean' in backfill spec (defaults to false). If false and policy changes, the job will auto-pause.
Arjun: Decision recap: pause current affected jobs; snapshot saved; implement resume API with mode (normal|canary|forced), policy/runtime fingerprint checks, operator override with logged reason; add tenant opt-in flag; and follow up with staged_rollout RFC.
Zoe: I'll post the mock and copy in the ticket.
Miguel: Pushed runtime_fingerprint changes to staging, will wire into job metadata by EOD.
Sam: I'll sketch the resume API and audit schema in the API repo.
ops-bot: reminder: affected tenants notified via email for paused backfills.
Arjun: Thanks team. Let's avoid making autopolicy rollouts a surprise for long-running ops moving forward. End.
